quest.title: The Phantom Thief's Reappearance
quest.description: The bustling streets of the Court of Fontaine seem more lively than usual. Why not take a walk around?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x525, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I see! So you believe that this warning letter was sent by The Phantom Weasel?

dialogues.speaker: Abagnale
dialogues.text: Absolutely! I've said it before, and I'll say it again: The Phantom Weasel never acts as you expect. He must have faked his own death ten years ago using a body double!

dialogues.speaker: Abagnale
dialogues.text: Now that he's back, I'm sure the Gardes who worked on his case back in the day are in for a headache. But however this turns out in the end, the one thing it won't be is boring!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Couldn't agree more! As a journalist, I'm gonna get a lot of mileage out of this one!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Thank you, Sir, for your time. Now, whom should I interview next... Huh!? Hey, what a coincidence. Fancy meeting you here!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Perfect timing. So, The Phantom Weasel's latest warning letter — what are your thoughts?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, this is the first time we're hearing of this one. Could you clue us in?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Huh? Oh... Ah, sorry! Yes, this case is from a decade ago. I guess you wouldn't know about it...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Well, not to worry — you're in good hands, because I'm a professional! The story goes like this...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Ten or so years ago, a phantom thief became active in the Court of Fontaine. Known only as "The Weasel," nobody knew his true identity, and the authorities never managed to catch him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, cool! He sounds like one of those... mysterious night burglars that you read about in novels!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Precisely — well, except the part where they actually have a good reputation. Our Weasel targeted whatever people held dear, and no one was safe from his predations!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: He would just as soon steal a necklace from a rich merchant's safe as he would a toy doll given to a commoner child for their birthday.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like an absolute weirdo.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: I know! The phantom thieves you read about in novels rob the rich to pay the poor, but this guy did not discriminate. Unsurprisingly, this didn't work wonders for his public reputation. Every man and his dog wanted to see him behind bars.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeesh. So, uh... Did they catch him?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Umm... Not exactly. There's a good chance that the Weasel would still be at large to this day if it hadn't been for an accident ten years ago.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: A magician named Cesar fell to his death in a botched high-altitude escape performance.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: When the police went through his personal effects, they found a hoard of stolen loot and gadgets used for criminal activities... and that was how The Phantom Weasel's identity was revealed to all.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Sure enough, thefts in Fontaine went down after Cesar's death... But today, ten years on, the notorious thief has once again issued one of his warning letters — and pasted it on the gate of the Opera Epiclese for all to see!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: I had to squeeze through the crowd this morning to get a photo as soon as I heard... Here, it's this one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So this is the warning letter, huh? Let's see what he wrote...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Three days from now, when evening falls, I shall take from you that which you hold most dear at the opera house, just as you did to me ten years ago."

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: This is, without a doubt, a clear declaration of criminal intent. After years of laying low, The Phantom Weasel is back with a vengeance!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: What once seemed like an open-and-shut case has been blown wide open again. But why has he re-emerged now, and what does he want? I sense an epic scoop — and I'm going for it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-oh... If this thief will steal anything that other people value, does that mean even we might be targeted?

choices.text: He might steal all your favorite snacks.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Hmph, let him try! In fact... Paimon's gonna eat all her snacks right now — let's see what he can do about that!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Okay, the people have spoken. It's clear that the public are very concerned about The Phantom Weasel's reappearance...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Let's see, I've got a photo of the letter, my interview notes... Yup, that should be enough to form the skeleton of my article. It does feel like something is missing, though...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Something... exclusive.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Who should I interview next? I need someone with a more concrete connection to the Weasel... Hmm? Is that who I think it is...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lyney?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Looks like he's performing some magic.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Magic... Magician... Cesar... The Phantom Weasel! That's it! Let's go interview Lyney!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: You see? The original phantom thief, Cesar, was a magician too. And what do phantom thieves and magicians have in common? They both have an air of mystery about them! Perhaps there's a connection there?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you serious? What sort of a deduction is that!?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Oh, relax... My journalistic instinct tells me that an exclusive news story is beckoning. Let's go — no time for delay!

choices.text: He might try to nab you, little Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aww... But Paimon doesn't wanna get kidnapped... Well, he'd have to go through you first. ...You would stop him, right?

dialogues.speaker: David
dialogues.text: Wow, Mr. Magician! How did you know which card I'd picked?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh, it's simple! Come closer, and I'll let you in on my secret... Magicians have a special skill called "telepathy," which means we can read other people's minds.

dialogues.speaker: David
dialogues.text: Really? Then... What am I thinking now?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, first you need to relax... Because I can see that you're clenching your fist in your mind, as if to say "No, I mustn't let him guess it..."

dialogues.speaker: David
dialogues.text: Aww...!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: And now you're getting a little flustered. You're trying to find a way to empty your mind, to think of nothing at all. But the more you try to hide a secret, the easier it'll come out~

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You snuck out from home today, didn't you? You told your family a little lie so you could come out and play. Now, now, that's not a good habit.

dialogues.speaker: David
dialogues.text: Y—You can tell? Oh boy... you really CAN read my mind!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Of course. And that's the end of my performance — you should really be heading home. Remember to apologize to your family, alright? They must be worried about you.

dialogues.speaker: David
dialogues.text: A—Alright, got it. Bye, Mr. Magician!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Hey, Lyney...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Why, hello, we meet again. Are you looking for me? What's the situation?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, why don't you guess, Mr. Telepathic?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh, please! You didn't believe that spiel, did you? The power of telepathy is quite beyond me.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I'm sure that child would beg to differ... Seemed like you were right on the money.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That was nothing more than a little trickery. I made an educated guess based on his microexpressions...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That, plus the fact that he was the only kid here without his parents, and he looked as guilty as sin. He made it easy for me.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You guys, on the other hand... Let me guess... Don't tell me you're here for the Phantom Weasel, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! Got it in one! Is this more of your trickery at work?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Wait, really? Haha... No, no trickery this time. It was pure luck.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: His warning letter's been the talk of the town, so I figured that maybe you were asking around about that.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Bingo! I plan on writing a column reporting on the latest news about The Phantom Weasel!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: So Lyney, what are your thoughts on this infamous thief's reappearance?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hmm... To be honest, it makes me angry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Angry? Why?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You read his letter, right? The Phantom Weasel claims he's planning something in three nights' time at the opera house. That's the night I'll be performing there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, what are the chances...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Wait a minute. You don't think he's after you... do you?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, if he is, then his warning is clearly a direct challenge to me personally.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: And if he's not... then it's still going to be a huge headache for me.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The mere mention of the Weasel's name is enough to scare people off. So once the contents of that letter get out, barely anyone will be showing up to watch my show.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But I've been preparing for this for a long time. I'm not about to let him ruin my big day. This leaves me with only one choice... I have to expose The Phantom Weasel's identity before the show begins.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Really? So what you're saying is... We might get to see a live duel between a famous magician and an infamous thief? Wow... This has "exclusive" written all over it!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: To be honest, I'm not sure if I'll emerge the victor. The Phantom Weasel is a notorious crook, infamous for his inscrutable methods.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: You're being far too modest, Lyney. I think your magic tricks are even more inscrutable than those of a thief!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Thanks for the compliment, though I have to say, I don't care much for the comparison.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: A lot of people liken magicians to thieves because we both have the ability to make things disappear without the person noticing. But there's an important difference that these people overlook.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Allow me to demonstrate with a quick magic trick. Here I have a flower, just an ordinary flower that was picked not long ago. Watch it carefully now... Three, two, one...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's gone!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where'd it go?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That's the question. Where did it go?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Therein lies the difference between us. Thieves make precious things disappear, but only magicians make them reappear.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: If I could now invite you all to check your clothes... There might be a surprise in there somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A surprise? Lemme see...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's right there! But how? You haven't moved this whole time!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: What an outstanding trick! Sorry, Lyney, it seems that my previous praise was woefully inadequate. Clearly, magic is the superior art form to theft.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I didn't take offense. I just wanted to take the opportunity to perhaps change some of the preconceived notions you might have about magicians.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Since Cesar's death, a lot of people associate magicians with criminality. It can be quite frustrating.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I can imagine. Um, coming back to your trick just now — might I presume that you are well-versed in floral symbolism?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: For example, magicians often use "Rainbow Roses" in their flower-related performances to represent "passion" and "romantic encounters."

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: But you used a Lumidouce Bell, which, if I'm not mistaken, allude to "separations." I'm curious to know if there was any deeper meaning behind this choice?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Impressive knowledge — it's no wonder you're such a successful journalist. But I'm afraid I don't know the first thing about floral symbolism. I'm just in the habit of using Lumidouce Bells in my magic.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: It sounds like something I should look into though. I'll buy myself a copy of "Fontaine's Floral Language Facts" when I have some time — but it'll have to wait until this Phantom Weasel business is behind us.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Well-noted... In that case, this brings us to the end of our interview. I, for one, am looking forward to the final showdown between you and the thief.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Please feel free to get in touch to update me on any further developments. Otherwise, I will of course see you at your show in three days' time. But let's hope The Phantom Weasel is caught by then.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: If there's nothing else, I'll be off. You've given me lots to work with here, and I've got no time to lose if I wanna write that exclusive piece! I'll see you all later!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Lyney... Are you gonna tell us how you did that flower trick now?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hehe... I'm afraid that's my little secret.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww... Well, magicians are entitled to their secrets... But Paimon's reeeally itching to know how it's done...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You feel it too, right? So itchy!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hehe, not so itchy then, huh?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Well, since you're so concerned, how would you like to serve as my temporary magician's assistants, and help me investigate?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Magician's assistants? That sounds fun! Assistants are technically magicians too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, it'll bring us one step closer to figuring out how that darn trick is done! Shall we go for it?

choices.text: We'll help you with your investigation.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Excellent. Thank you for putting your trust in moi.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: The first thing we need to look into is who Cesar really was. If he truly was The Phantom Weasel, that means that the weasel is dead, and whoever wrote this warning letter is just a copycat criminal.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But if he wasn't The Weasel... Well, that'll make things more interesting. It would mean that The Weasel lives, and he's been laying low all this time in some corner of Fontaine.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: And if we're investigating Cesar, his fiancée, Jemma, is a good place to start. Word is that she visits the cemetery often, so I asked Lynette to wait for her there.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: We should make a move. Let's go and rendezvous with Lynette.

choices.text: You sure you'll be able to handle him?

talks.objective: Go to the cemetery to look for Jemma

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: ...You took your time.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #Sorry. I bumped into {NICKNAME} and Charlotte en route, and we ended up chatting for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been a while, Lynette!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're working as Lyney's temporary assistants in the investigation of The Phantom Weasel!

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Thank you. It's good to have you helping.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: So, what's the situation? Have you seen Jemma?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Nope. I've been here a while, and she still hasn't shown up.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: How bizarre. Maybe it was bad intel?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #Well, we won't get anywhere by standing around waiting. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, let's go ask around.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Excuse me good sir, do you by any chance know a Jemma?

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: Jemma? You mean Cesar's fiancée? Sure I do... What's this about?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I'm just trying to get ahold of her, because I need her help with something. I heard she comes here a lot?

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: Yeah, she does. *sigh* Poor thing... It's no secret why, either. She's heartsick.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: Ever since Cesar passed away, she's been coming here once every week to clean his grave. Often, she just sits there in front of his headstone, lost in thought. Sometimes she talks to herself.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: I asked her what she was doing once. She said... she wanted to speak to him again.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: She knows he's gone, and can't hear her from the grave, but... She just likes to spend time there, telling her fiancé all about how her life is going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And she's been doing this ever since Cesar passed away? So, ten years? Wow. Their love must've been really strong.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: I'll bet. Cesar's reputation fell apart after his identity was revealed, so no one else visits his grave... Jemma's the only one who still thinks about him after all these years.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: I don't know if the mind lives on in the waters after death, but if it does... I'm sure Cesar must be grateful to have someone who remembers him fondly.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: If I'm honest, I think this is all so unfair to poor Jemma. Her fiancé was a lowlife crook — he doesn't deserve someone like her.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: Anyway, all of that said — she's running later than usual today. Normally, she'd be sitting in front of his grave by now. I wonder if she's okay?

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: Well, that's everything I know, I'm afraid. You might have more luck asking some other people.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Alright, well thanks for sharing all of this with us. We'll keep asking around.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: You're welcome. *sigh* ...I just hope she'll be able to move on one day.

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: Did you hear the news? They're saying The Phantom Weasel's back.

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: You're kidding... Wait, isn't he dead?

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: I dunno anymore. All sorts of news flying around nowadays. I can never tell what's true and what isn't.

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: But what if... Just hypothetically, I mean... What if this Weasel's the real deal, and Cesar was framed?

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: Called it. Seriously, ten years ago, on the day it all went down, I said to myself "You know what? This guy's been set up." The Cesar I knew was a good guy. He gave balloons to children on the street, for Pete's sake. What, are we supposed to believe that he was a balloon thief, or something? Gimme a break.

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: Oh please. Weren't you the one cursing his name to high heaven when the police announced the news!? You were all, "That gosh-darn lousy son of a... You think you know a guy..." Or words to that effect.

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: Wait, did I say that? Hmm. I don't seem to recall...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry to interrupt...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hello there. Sorry for disturbing you, but I couldn't help but notice you were discussing The Phantom Weasel?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We're actually quite interested in this topic as well, but we're struggling to get to the bottom of it. Do you think you could spare a moment to tell us a little bit about Cesar?

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: You've come to the right people. Yep... I was there. Back when Cesar used to perform magic tricks on the street.

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: He was a great magician. The best trick I ever saw him do was pop a transparent balloon, only for a whole bunch of doves to fly out from the inside.

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: I was right up close and didn't blink or look away once. But for the life of me, I still don't have the faintest clue how he pulled it off. Really incredible stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: I saw him perform too. He always used to bring some gifts along for the kids who came to watch his show, and he'd hand them out after he was done.

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: Sometimes, he even got the kids to write their wishes down, and then he'd make the items on the "wishlist" appear in his next show.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, he doesn't sound like such a bad guy...

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: But after he died, there were also rumors that he used the wishlist to find out what was precious to people, with the intent to steal it later.

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: ...As I'm sure you know, The Phantom Weasel would steal just about anything from anyone.

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, now that The Weasel is back, Cesar's become a hot topic once more.

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: I bet Jemma must be pleased. If Cesar's name gets cleared, maybe it'll finally give her some solace after all this time.

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: Oh, speak of the devil — that's her over there. If you've got any more questions about Cesar, she's definitely the one to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's Jemma... Is it just Paimon, or does it look like something's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... It looks like she's injured! C'mon, let's see if she's okay!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Hi there. You're Jemma, right?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: ...Who's asking?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Don't be afraid, we mean no harm.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: It looks like you're injured. How bad is it?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: Thanks for your concern, but you didn't answer my question. Who are you? And what do you want with me?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: My name is Lyney, and this is my sister Lynette.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #My name's Paimon, and this here's {NICKNAME}. We're investigating The Phantom Weasel.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The Weasel posted a warning letter this morning. If he still lives, that means that Cesar was falsely accused.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You knew Cesar better than anyone else. So if you're willing, we'd love to hear what you think about all this.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I promise you can trust us. We won't hurt you — in fact, we'll do all we can to keep you safe.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: I... I never believed that he was The Weasel.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Huh, I suspected as much. Okay, so going back ten years, do you remember anything strange in the weeks leading up to the accident? Did Cesar have a falling out with anyone, for instance?

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: ...No. Not that I know of.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Got it. Alright, sorry for disturbing you.

dialogues.speaker: Jemma
dialogues.text: If you don't have any more questions, please leave. I want to be alone with him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Judging by the look on her face, there's definitely something fishy about her...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: She's lying. She definitely knows something.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Perhaps she simply doesn't trust us.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That's fair. We're just a bunch of strangers who showed up and started questioning her about things that happened a whole decade ago... It makes sense that she'd be wary around us.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: In any case, I doubt we'll get any further here, so let's call it a day. Meet me outside Hotel Debord tomorrow, and then we'll start the next step of our plan.

dialogues.speaker: Gracia
dialogues.text: A lot of people here today, huh. When did this cemetery get so popular?

dialogues.speaker: Juliano
dialogues.text: Same thoughts here. What's going on...

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: A lot of people find cemeteries bleak and oppressive, but not me.

dialogues.speaker: Baltasar
dialogues.text: I find the silence gives me a sense of peace. And something about being in the presence of the dead and buried... It sorta puts all of life's woes in perspective.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: I'll wait for you here and see if Jemma shows up.
